newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania launches much awaited OTC market.
newsitem.headline: Romania launches much awaited OTC market.

text.p: Romania took one more step towards a free market system on Friday when a long-awaited over-the-counter (OTC) trading system went on stream to handle shares from the ex-communist country's mass selloff scheme.

"This is a historic moment, the crowning of the mass privatisation programme which opens a new page in the practice of market economy," Romanian President Ion Iliescu said, pressing a computer key at a ceremony to launch the system.

The RASDAQ system, modelled on the U.S. NASDAQ exchange and developed under a $21 million capital market project run by the U.S. Agency for International Development, will undergo 30 days of testing. Actual trading will start by end-October.

"During this testing period orders will be collected and stocks to enter trading on this market will be taken from a pre-selected batch of around 150 companies," said Septimiu Stoica, president of the RASDAQ SRL administration board.

The RASDAQ is expected to eventually trade shares in some 5,000 medium-sized companies, most of them privatised under the mass selloff, through 74 dealers and brokers and some 300 work stations across the country.

Under an ambitious scheme launched in October 1995, 17 million Romanians were invited to swap coupons for around 600 million shares in some 4,000 state companies. The process ended in March with a subscription percentage of around 90 percent.

The OTC market, which missed two previous deadlines due to poor infrastructure and problems in creating a share registry, is expected to break the hold the state still has on industry and to attract much-needed foreign investment.
Stock brokers say the OTC system is a needed addition to the capital market as the young Bucharest bourse lost stamina over the last few months and only trades 13 stocks.
The OTC is also hailed by Romania's 12 investment funds which say the OTC market gives fund managers the investment tools they need to develop.

"This (the OTC system) is a clear signal that economic reform is progressing at an accelerated pace," Finance Minister Florin Georgescu told Reuters Television at Monday's ceremony. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
